evidence: Built tamper_harness.py, which exercises the live mechanisms rather than models of them: the manifests emit_result.py wrote, and verify_chain imported from workstreams/po03/tools/transactional_factory.py with its module roots repointed at a scratch tree. Executed it: PO03_TAMPER_PASS cases=15 detected=9 clean=4 known_undetected=2, exit 0, captured verbatim in evidence/tamper-run.txt. Nine mutations were caught with the verifier's real messages: flipping one byte of a materialised artifact changed its SHA-256 from a15363b7419e2937 to 6f1070206cecb595; truncating it changed measured bytes from 2600 to 1300; rewriting one manifest entry changed the manifest hash from the 4a6a53368f1a7587 the result cites to 9f4c08ed0f4f289c; mutating an event body produced 'event hash mismatch' plus 'previous hash mismatch' on the successor; a length-preserving single-byte flip (388 bytes before and after) was still caught; deleting a middle event produced 'non-monotonic sequence'; overwriting an event's own event_sha256 was caught; rewriting previous_event_sha256 and recomputing the event's own hash was still caught because the link is to the predecessor's file hash; and a copy of the real po03-canary-001 chain verified clean with errors=[] then failed once one actor field was edited. Four pristine states verified clean, which is what makes the nine detections non-vacuous. Separately, copying every event directory the repository holds into a scratch tree and running the real verify_chain over all of them produced no errors, and tampering five of those copies made each fail. Ran python3 -I -m unittest discover over the unit subtree: 24 tests, OK, exit 0, captured in evidence/test-run.txt.
falsifiable_hypothesis: Mutating a committed artifact after the fact breaks the manifest and the event hash chain.
limitations: Two tamper shapes are confirmed UNDETECTED by verify_chain and are recorded as gaps with tests that fail if the behaviour changes. Deleting the tail event leaves a chain that is internally consistent, so truncation is invisible; nothing records the chain's expected head. Appending a forged event with correct links also verifies, because a hash chain constrains order and not authorship, so any actor able to write under control/events can extend history. Closing either needs an external anchor or a signature, neither of which a producer may install.

A committed artifact cannot be mutated in place at all: after corrupting the working copy, git cat-file returned the original bytes and hash (identical=True). The hypothesis is therefore only testable as history rewriting, which changes object ids and breaks every git:<commit>:<path> locator, or as a new commit, which leaves the locator pointing at the original bytes. The manifest's strength here comes from git's content addressing as much as from the recorded hash.

The harness repoints the factory module's REPO_ROOT, PO03_ROOT, CONTROL_ROOT and RECEIPT_ROOT after import because those are computed at module level from __file__; that is what lets the real verifier run over scratch bytes but couples the harness to those four names.

Detection of a manifest mutation is shown by measurement, not by invoking a gate; the gate that would refuse such a manifest in CI is unit 029's coverage_assert.py. Only the first artifact of the first manifested slot is corrupted, since the tamper classes are properties of hashing rather than of a particular file.
